problem: DRL crowd navigation policies use oversimplified scene representations: pedestrians as 2D points (position/velocity) and environments as 2D occupancy maps or single-line lidar. They discard visual cues such as body pose and environment semantics, which limits real-world generalization.
motivation: Humans reveal intentions through head, shoulder and body pose before changing direction, and constrained spaces require awareness of structure. End-to-end raw-image-to-action mapping suffers from dimensionality and gives no guarantee that social context is captured. A compact BEV representation, augmented with pose-based intention features, should support foresighted DRL decisions.
key_idea: Build intention-aware scene representations by concatenating a spatio-temporal BEV occupancy embedding from RGB-D with an attention-based embedding of 3D human poses (I2Former), and train a PPO policy on them.
insight: Both components matter: removing either lowers SR and raises time in pedestrians' private zones (TPZ) in nearly all scenes (e.g. High-density warehouse SR 0.80 full vs 0.75 w/o I2 vs 0.73 w/o BEV; office long-horizon 0.95 vs 0.80 / 0.83). Pose-based intention mainly reduces private-zone intrusion, while BEV provides structural awareness. BEV alone (w/o I2) already roughly matches DRL-VO, which needs a full map, pedestrian states and LiDAR. A simple reward suffices because the representation encodes intent.
method: Spatio-temporal encoder: Fiery-style pipeline where ResNet-18 features from 2 RGB-D cameras are lifted with depth, sum-pooled into a 120x200 BEV map, aligned across T past frames by ego-motion, and fused by a 3D-conv temporal encoder pre-trained on nuScenes.
BEV encoder: 2D residual CNN with pooling maps the spatio-temporal BEV features to the embedding z_bev.
Pose extraction: YOLO 2D pose detection lifted to 3D (17 joints x N pedestrians) in the robot frame using depth and camera parameters; occluded keypoints are zero-padded.
IntentFormer: MLP pose encoder followed by multi-head self-attention over joints, FFN, residual and LayerNorm, then attention pooling to give a per-pedestrian intention feature.
InteractFormer: multi-head cross-attention with the robot state embedding as query over pedestrian intention features, giving z_interact.

Feature fusion + PPO: concatenate z_bev, z_interact and the robot state embedding (goal direction, distance, velocity), fuse with an MLP, and train with PPO. The RGB backbone and temporal encoder stay frozen. Reward: +20 goal, -20 collision, a proximity penalty, a progress term, and an angular-velocity smoothing penalty.
SocNav-Gym: Isaac Sim environments with SFM-driven animated pedestrians for training (hallways, corners, clutter, open crowds) and testing (office, hospital, warehouse).

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 (frozen, pre-trained) + 3D-conv temporal encoder (frozen, nuScenes pre-trained) + trained BEV CNN, I2Former transformers and MLPs; PPO policy
setting.training_data: Online PPO in Isaac Sim SocNav-Gym; nuScenes pre-training for the temporal encoder and ResNet-18 pre-trained weights
setting.observation: Two RGB-D cameras (RealSense D435, ~140° combined FOV), YOLO 3D human poses, robot state (goal, velocity)
setting.action_space: continuous linear and angular velocity commands (max 1.0 m/s)
setting.privileged: none at test time for the policy (the topological map for long-horizon tests is generated via a generalized Voronoi graph)

numbers.extra: 3 trials x 25 random goals; density 0.1 ped/m2; width 7.0 m
numbers.evidence: Table 1, Comparison Results in Simulated Crowd Navigation, Low, Office Lobby

numbers_note: Custom Isaac Sim benchmark, not a standard navigation benchmark. Ablation variants (w/o I2, w/o BEV) and baselines are in the tables but omitted here. Real-world results are qualitative (109.49 m mall run, average speed 0.76 m/s, 15 Hz inference).
results: iCrowdNav achieves the highest SR in all six simulated scene/density settings (e.g. 0.95 in the low-density office lobby, 0.80 in the high-density warehouse) and the lowest TPZ. In high-density scenes it beats DRL-VO, SARL*-OM, ViNT and DWA (warehouse: 0.80 vs 0.71 / 0.57 / 0.51 / 0.72). In long-horizon tests it reaches SR 0.95 in the office vs 0.75 for DRL-VO, and 0.79 in the hospital vs 0.67. Zero-shot sim-to-real deployment works in a gym, a subway station and a mall.
limitations: Severe occlusions and the limited field of view of egocentric cameras make intention inference difficult in ultra-dense scenes.
Evaluated on a self-built simulator with SFM-driven pedestrians and small trial counts (3x25), so the pedestrian model may not match real crowd behaviour; real-world results are only qualitative.
Depends on the reliability of the external pose detector and depth for 3D lifting.
builds_on: Trajectron++ style pose-based intention (Salzmann et al.)
